title: Travelling by bus after his accident, cars in Europe
summary: Herman has ridden the bus more in two years than in his whole career because of his accident; in Europe he has a car and driver.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I was asking about that. He ought to do it again. Okay. Did you travel early on on the bus with everybody?
At different periods, but never a great
deal. I've done more travel on the bus in the last two years than I have probably in my entire career.
Now, why is that, because of your --

Because of my accident and so forth. And the weather does a lot of things as far as air travel is concerned. Chicago has been seeing a great deal of this winter already. And consequently it's been easier for me, because of not being able to get around too well and so on.

To do the bus routine. And I can handle it for about three or four, five days or six days without taking a break. And -- if the jumps are reasonable. But ordinarily, they are not reasonable, as we spoke about earlier. And that's why I can only last a very few days, and then I have to fly for a few days. Then that gets terribly boring.
Then you get back on again.

Then I get back on again, yeah, because the one distinct advantage is getting out of your motel or hotel in the morning, jumping on the bus and not having to worry about a thing until you arrive at your next destination.
And you don't have to look for cabs and all that.
What about in Europe? Do you ride busses there, too? I was just wondering, in other countries?

Not very much, no. I have an arrangement with the impresario or the guy who handles the tours for me that ordinarily I have a car at my disposal, and -- with a driver, because I find it makes my life a lot more comfortable and I come and go as I please. I can do a lot more things that I could possible do if I had to travel with the band every day.
